capability_map.capability: Persistent identity lock: train one real (or invented) person once and reuse the face across every still and into video
capability_map.since: Soul ID help page dated 2026-08-01 (feature older); carries into Seedance as an Element
capability_map.what_it_admits: A licensed twin of a real working model built from 20–80 photos in minutes, reused for hundreds of catalogue/e-commerce images. Limits stated by the vendor: 'clearly the same person' not pixel-identical; identity NOT exportable (vendor lock-in); requires the person's permission. In 2024 one person could not hold a face across a catalogue cycle without a shoot.

capability_map.capability: Multi-reference image generation/editing holding several people and products
capability_map.what_it_admits: 'Up to 14 images… consistency and resemblance of up to 5 people' — a catalogue spread with a recurring cast and exact supplied packshots in one pass; group/family scenes.

capability_map.capability: In-context editing that preserves supplied assets (image and video)
capability_map.what_it_admits: Restyle/relight/re-scene a real product or garment photo without regenerating it; swap people in existing footage (Aleph: https://runwayml.com/research/introducing-runway-aleph). Makes 'composite the real packshot, never generate the label' a workable QA rule.

capability_map.capability: Multimodal reference video with native audio: many images + clips + audio in, 15–30 s multi-shot out
capability_map.since: 2026-02-12 (Seedance 2.0: 9 img/3 video/3 audio); 2026-07-31 (Seedance 2.5: 30 s one-take, 30 img/10 video/10 audio refs); Veo 3.1 audio in Ingredients-to-Video 2025-10-15
capability_map.what_it_admits: A single operator can make a 30-s catwalk/lookbook or reseller reel with a consistent licensed person, the exact product and voice, without a crew. Veo: https://blog.google/technology/ai/veo-updates-flow/ ; Kling 3.0 multi-shot (up to 6 cuts) + Elements — release-note date UNVERIFIED (JS page).

capability_map.capability: Garment virtual try-on as an API with explicit moderation control
capability_map.since: FASHN v1.6 docs (fetched 2026-09-25); Google Doppl 2025-06-26; Google Merchant Center auto opt-in apparel try-on
capability_map.what_it_admits: Flat-lay/ghost photo → on-model image per SKU at ~US$0,10/credit; 'permissive' default ALLOWS swimwear/underwear (kills the 'lingerie gap' seed). Also means the buyer can self-serve: WearView US$29, VestiAI R$159,90/80 photos, Mercado Livre free 'Gerar fotos com IA'.

capability_map.capability: Automatic dubbing with voice clone in 90+ languages
capability_map.what_it_admits: A licensed spokesperson/ambassador twin can speak localized offers (per city, per franchise unit) or other languages with lip-sync; also a self-serve front door (HeyGen US$29–149/month: https://www.heygen.com/pricing).

capability_map.capability: Agents that operate a browser / run a vendor's production recipe end to end
capability_map.since: 2025-08-25 Claude in Chrome pilot (expanded Nov–Dec 2025); Higgsfield MCP workflows (HIGGSFIELD_FACTS.md)
capability_map.what_it_admits: Batch production (brief → generate → auto-filter → QA checklist) runs unattended; her hours go to casting, selection and client calls. It is a COST-of-operating gain, not a right to charge: the same recipe is available to every in-house marketer (C4 still forbids her operating inside client systems).

capability_map.capability: Published done-for-you AI fashion production price in São Paulo (market capability, not a model)
capability_map.what_it_admits: The replacement-cost ceiling is now a price list: R$35 per 3 lookbook images, R$80–120/look with video, R$53 per AI persona, R$53 per campaign image, R$260 per 15–20 s video. Any AI-production candidate in her domain must price against it.

candidates.name: CICLO — the reseller-catalogue image desk for direct-sales beauty, lingerie and fashion brands (a sharper VBPH: same machine, buyer with a clock)
candidates.shape: S5 production-on-a-consumption-clock (named as a deliberate sharpening of VBPH: the buyer is not a launching brand but a catalogue whose 'ciclo/campanha' forces the next order)
candidates.one_line: Every 3–6 weeks a direct-sales company must publish a new revista/campanha for its resellers; Sol supplies the on-model/lifestyle layer (60–90 images + 4 reseller reels) with a recurring catalogue cast and composited real packshots, to the gráfica deadline, at ~R$4.500 per revista.
candidates.who_pays: Marketing/catálogo heads of mid-size venda-direta companies (DeMillus, Abelha Rainha, Racco, Mahogany, Odorata, Hinode, Amakha Paris, Moments Paris, Mawwal, Avatim, Água de Cheiro, Skelt, Zyone, Crystallini, Hiroshima, Quatro Estações, Dicorpo, Sawary…). Not Natura/Avon/Boticário-group/L'Occitane/Granado (assumed in-house, UNVERIFIED).
candidates.observed_money: CLEARING anchor (SP studio, published): AI campaign image R$53/image, 15–20 s video R$260, lookbook image R$11,67 (R$35/3) — Estúdio Fábrica. A 60-image + 4-reel pack at those rates = R$4.220. ASKING ceiling: SINAPRO-MS 2025 agency list — catalogue cover R$7.404,20, miolo ≤16 pp R$22.435,18, social post R$4.008,37, WhatsApp card R$4.461,72 (list warns >50% discounts occur). Per-revista imagery spend of any named company: UNVERIFIED.
candidates.why_demand_repeats: The ciclo is a CONSUMPTION CLOCK the buyer does not control after launch and cannot stretch: DeMillus published 9 revistas covering 19 campanhas in 2025 (Revendi listing); Jequiti cycle ~21 days (SECONDARY); Abelha Rainha 4 campanhas listed for 2026 so far (BR Catálogos). One yes = 6–17 orders a year without re-origination.
candidates.what_she_does_on_a_tuesday: 09:00 brief for Revista 19-01 arrives (product grid, supplied packshots, promo themes). 10:00 casts from the brand's 3 recurring catalogue faces (licensed twins or owned synthetic personas), runs batch generation via the Higgsfield/Nano Banana Pro recipe, composites the real packshots (labels never generated). 14:00 QA against the product truth sheet; 16:00 20-min video call with the catalogue coordinator to approve heroes; ships print-ready CMYK + 4 vertical reels. ~15–20 h per pack.
candidates.tool_vendor_front_door: OPEN: an in-house designer can run Higgsfield's product-photoshoot recipe at US$49/month, and Estúdio Fábrica already sells done-for-you at R$53/image. What she sells that the vendor does not: guaranteed volume on a print deadline every ciclo, casting continuity across ciclos (same faces, same light), print-resolution compositing (the vendor's own recipe says it cannot verify tiny text or full-res sharpness), and a no-invented-efficacy claim check (CONAR 2026 makes advertiser and agency jointly liable for AI content — SECONDARY).
candidates.treadmill_verdict: BETTER for 12–24 months (each release cuts her cost per revista), then drifts OBSOLETE wherever the buyer has an in-house designer who learns the recipe. Durable only where volume × deadline × continuity is the product, not the pixels.
candidates.first_20_calls: DeMillus, Abelha Rainha, Racco, Mahogany, Odorata, Hinode, Jequiti, Amakha Paris, Moments Paris, Mawwal, Avatim, Água de Cheiro, Skelt, Farmasi (BR), Zyone, Crystallini, Hiroshima, Quatro Estações, Dicorpo, Sawary — ask for the gerente de marketing / coordenação de catálogo (names from ABEVD member list, Revendi and BR Catálogos).
candidates.pool_estimate: ≈R$810.000/yr (hypothesis, two of three multipliers partly verified)
candidates.pool_derivation: ~20 addressable mid-size catalogue brands (≈33 beauty/fashion catalogue brands across Revendi 29 + ABEVD 22 + BR Catálogos, minus in-house giants — UNVERIFIED who is in-house) × 9 revistas/yr (DeMillus verified; others 4–17 UNVERIFIED) × R$4.500/pack (Fábrica-rate bill of materials R$4.220).
candidates.pool_div4_vs_bar: R$810k ÷ 4 = R$202k/yr vs bar ≈R$160–200k/yr gross (net R$10.500–13.000/mo at ~14% tax + ~8% tools) — PASSES AT THE EDGE. Needs 4–5 clients at DeMillus cadence (R$40.500/client/yr) or 2–3 at a 17-ciclo cadence. Hours: 3–3,75 packs/month × ~18 h + 15 h sales/admin = 69–83 h of 87.
candidates.revealed_preferences_traded: Keeps ORIGINATION ONCE (the ciclo re-orders by itself) and the machine makes the unit; trades MACHINE-TEST limb 3 — she holds 2–5 marketing-team relationships and a proof call per revista. Compensated by a hard consumption clock, beauty/lingerie/fashion domain, and a sale made by Portuguese calls.
candidates.biggest_flaw: Unknown whether mid-size catalogue brands buy imagery outside (in-house studios are plausible) and at what per-revista price; and cosmetic labels/lingerie lace are exactly where generation fails at print resolution.
candidates.repair: (1) Sell only the MODEL/LIFESTYLE layer — the costliest part of a revista — and leave packshots and page layout to the in-house team, so she is additive not a replacement. (2) Hard rule: labels are always composited from the brand's supplied packshots, never generated; lingerie lace/prints are try-on-from-real-garment (FASHN permissive) with a human QA pass. (3) Price per revista, invoiced, no retainer, so a lost ciclo costs nothing to either side.
candidates.next_test: (a) R$0 desk test this week: pull the last 3 revistas of 10 catalogue brands from Revendi/BR Catálogos and count on-model/lifestyle images and distinct faces per revista. (b) Then 20 Portuguese calls to the list above asking who produces the revista imagery, how many images per ciclo, and what one revista's model layer costs today; offer a paid pilot of one revista.
candidates.bar: (a) median ≥40 on-model/lifestyle images per revista in ≥6 of 10 brands (else the unit is too small to matter). (b) ≥5 of 20 calls name a supplier and a per-revista spend ≥R$5.000, AND ≥2 accept a paid pilot at ≥R$3.500 within 45 days. Below either bar: kill.

candidates.name: GÊMEO LICENCIADO — the twin department for São Paulo model agencies (licensed real-model twins booked by brands)
candidates.shape: S6+S5 hybrid: matches a consented real face (talent side) to a brand booking, then a machine makes the unit
candidates.one_line: Sol builds and operates LGPD-consented, contract-cleared digital twins of working-level agency models, so a brand can 'book' a real, cleared face for an e-commerce/catalogue set without a shoot day; the model and agency are paid the usage fee, Sol invoices production and twin management.
candidates.who_pays: Brands (e-commerce/catalogue buyers) pay the model/agency usage fee directly (pass-through, off her books) and pay Sol production (~R$2.900 at Fábrica rates) + twin management/clearance (~R$500) per digital booking. Agencies are the channel and co-sellers.
candidates.observed_money: Talent side: signed SATED-SP/SIAESP CCT 2026–27 pisos per 8 h diária — internet video protagonist R$600, TV/streaming protagonist R$1.438,14 (actors; models' own CCT still in negotiation). Standard SP e-commerce booking licenses 'direito de imagem de 1 ano' (Job for Model). Synthetic alternative priced at R$53 per AI persona (Estúdio Fábrica). H&M pays twin usage 'exactly the same' as a normal job (CNN, SECONDARY). Terra's '30% diária / 70% usage' split is SECONDARY/UNVERIFIED.
candidates.why_demand_repeats: Per-booking, not per-subscription: a brand that likes a twin books it again each collection; each agency that adopts the department feeds bookings without her originating every one. Unproven in Brazil.
candidates.what_she_does_on_a_tuesday: Morning: onboards a new model — capture spec (20–80 photos per Soul ID guidance, shot by the agency or the model), LGPD art. 11 specific consent + AI-derivative image licence (her template), trains the twin, runs a 12-image fidelity check the model approves. Afternoon: produces a booking (40 stills + 3 short films) for a brand, sends proofs to the booker. 17:00 30-min call with an agency director she has not yet signed.
candidates.tool_vendor_front_door: PARTLY CLOSED — the one input no tool vendor sells: a real person's consent. Higgsfield itself requires permission; a synthetic face costs R$53 (Fábrica) or nothing. But a brand could recruit a model and train Soul ID itself in 5 minutes; what it cannot cheaply get is agency-sanctioned AI-derivative terms, LGPD biometric consent on file, and a face whose image rights are cleared. Legal exposure she sells against: CC art. 20 + STJ Súmula 403 (indemnity for unauthorized commercial image use 'independe de prova do prejuízo').
candidates.treadmill_verdict: BETTER: every release improves twin fidelity and cuts production cost; the right to charge sits in consent contracts, which no model release supplies. Risk is not the treadmill but SUPPLY ABUNDANCE (thousands of models; any agency can do it — Joy announced 'Joy IA' in Apr 2025).
candidates.first_20_calls: Agencies: Joy Management (JOY ID dept, Fernando Herbert — the Joy IA coordinator), Way Model Management, Mega Models, Ford Models Brasil, Elite Brasil, Bossa; Job for Model (SP booking marketplace); Manager Fashion (the SaaS that powers Joy's site — one partnership reaches many agencies); remaining ~12 SP agencies to be listed by hand (models.com returns 403 here) plus 4–6 brands that book the same e-commerce face every collection.
candidates.pool_estimate: ≈R$816.000/yr — HYPOTHESIS (three stacked unverified multipliers), not a number
candidates.pool_derivation: 10 partner agencies × 2 twin bookings/month × R$3.400 to Sol × 12. Agencies' convertible booking volume, conversion to twin, and brand willingness to pay a real-face premium over a R$53 synthetic persona are all UNVERIFIED.
candidates.pool_div4_vs_bar: R$816k ÷ 4 = R$204k/yr vs bar ≈R$160–200k — passes only if 10 agencies each feed 2 bookings/month; needs 4–5 bookings/month total.
candidates.revealed_preferences_traded: Trades BOTH: origination is partly per booking and the business holds three-way relationships (model, agency, brand). Compensates with the strongest C8 fit in the lens (her talent-side grind knowledge: usage terms, agency norms, how a set runs) and the only input in the hunt the tool vendor cannot sell.
candidates.biggest_flaw: Demand is unproven in Brazil: a brand can get a free synthetic face, and Joy's announced platform is not visible on its site 17 months later (a first mover that apparently stalled).
candidates.repair: Sell the twin as the agencies' DEFENSIVE product (it keeps the 20% commission alive as shoot days shrink) and as a Súmula-403 clearance for brands, not as cheaper content. Start with brands that already book the same face every collection (continuity is the demand), price the model's usage like a normal job (H&M norm), and keep her fee to production + management so the agency's economics improve. Use Manager Fashion as a distribution partner rather than calling agencies one by one.
candidates.next_test: 20 Portuguese calls (list above): 'In 2026, has any client asked to use a model's image with AI, or asked for AI lookbooks with a real model? Would you pilot one twin with one consenting model and one existing client, usage paid as a normal booking?'
candidates.bar: ≥3 of 20 report at least one 2026 client request for AI/twin use of a real model, AND ≥2 agree to a co-funded pilot (one model, one brand booking) within 60 days. Fewer than 3 reported requests ⇒ kill: the demand does not exist yet.

candidates.name: COLEÇÃO DE REPRESENTANTE — per-collection digital lookbook + catwalk clips for trade-fair and rep-sold fashion labels (the wholesaler seed, tested)
candidates.shape: S5 per-collection production (seasonal clock); sharper buyer than Bom Retiro walk-in wholesale: labels that sell to multimarcas through reps and trade fairs, where 'the lojista buys from the catálogo'
candidates.one_line: From the label's flat/ghost photos of its pilot pieces, Sol delivers the collection on a consistent house model (stills + 11-s catwalk clip per look) and a line sheet reps can sell from — R$3.200 per 40 looks, ahead of Minas Trend / showroom season.
candidates.who_pays: Owners/commercial directors of fashion labels exhibiting at Minas Trend (>150 exhibitors/edition), labels recruiting sales reps (Santa Têxtil listings), and Bom Retiro/Brás/Goiânia/Fortaleza wholesale labels.
candidates.observed_money: Estúdio Fábrica (SP): AI lookbook + basic video ≤11 s R$80/look; + poses/angles ≤15 s R$120/look; AI lookbook R$35/3 images; physical half-day R$1.250 for ≤40 looks (model fee extra), catwalk video R$35. Self-serve: VestiAI R$159,90/80 photos (R$2/photo), Vitriny from R$3,68/image, WearView US$29/month, Mercado Livre free AI photos.
candidates.why_demand_repeats: Seasonal clock: every label launches ≥2 collections/yr (Minas Trend runs two editions; MT36 is 20–22 Oct 2026); wholesale labels in Brás/Bom Retiro drop far more often. Origination once per label, then per collection.
candidates.what_she_does_on_a_tuesday: Receives 40 flat-lay photos by WeTransfer from a Goiânia label; generates the looks on the label's house model with try-on-from-real-garment, renders 11-s catwalk clips (her runway eye on the walk), QA prints/drape against the flat photos, exports a line sheet PDF; calls 6 Minas Trend exhibitors.
candidates.tool_vendor_front_door: FULLY OPEN: Higgsfield Fashion Factory (one item + one character → photoset) in the US$49 plan, VestiAI R$2/photo with Brazilian models and PT-BR WhatsApp support, Mercado Livre's free 'Gerar fotos com IA' (the marketplace earns on the flow and gives production away), and a SP studio already selling done-for-you AI at R$35–120/look. She sells only turnaround, the walk, and taste.
candidates.treadmill_verdict: OBSOLETE: every release moves self-serve quality toward done-for-you quality; the price ceiling (R$80/look) is already published and falling.
candidates.first_20_calls: Minas Trend 33 womenswear exhibitors: Ateliê Ana Ribeiro, Conceito Alagoas, Fabiana Milazzo, Fernanda Buzo, Glória Morais, Janine Passini, Juliana Manzini, Lia Rabello, Moni, Neusa Faria, Pauzzi, Plié, Pontos e Contos, Premier, Raquel de Queiroz, Severa Fitness, Victoria, Bixugrillo, Cleo Schanen, Da Isadora (Instagram handles in the FIEMG PDF) — plus rep-recruiting labels from Santa Têxtil (Lady Lella, Mimos Confecções).
candidates.pool_derivation: ~450 reachable labels (≈150 Minas Trend exhibitors, primary + ~300 Bom Retiro/Brás/rep-recruiting labels, UNVERIFIED) × 2 collections/yr × R$3.200 (40 looks × R$80, the published SP done-for-you price).
candidates.pool_div4_vs_bar: R$2,9M ÷ 4 = R$720k/yr ≫ bar ≈R$160–200k — pool passes; the business fails on margin, not market. Needs 4–5 collections/month (170–210 looks) at ≤12 min/look to fit 87 h.
candidates.revealed_preferences_traded: Mostly keeps both: machine makes the unit, buyer verifies with own eyes, per-collection re-orders. Trades a small relationship per label. Domain: fashion + runway (C8 core).
candidates.biggest_flaw: A commodity with a published ceiling (R$80/look) and a R$2/photo self-serve floor; garment fidelity (drape, print scale) is where AI still misleads a B2B buyer, and a lojista who receives something unlike the image returns it.
candidates.repair: Sell the one thing a self-serve tool does not: timing and the walk — a 'coleção pronta para o salão' delivered 10 days before Minas Trend / showroom week, with catwalk clips directed by someone who walked runways, and a fidelity guarantee (re-render free if a rep reports a mismatch). Target labels whose buyers are 1.000 km away (multimarcas that cannot see the mostruário).
candidates.next_test: Before MT36 (20–22 Oct 2026): 20 Portuguese calls to the list offering 40 looks + 40 catwalk clips for R$3.200 delivered in 7 days; time the first real order end to end.
candidates.bar: ≥3 paid orders from 20 calls within 30 days AND measured production ≤12 min/look on the first order. Miss either ⇒ drop; it is a commodity she cannot win on price.

KEY FINDING FOR THE WHOLE HUNT: a São Paulo studio (Estúdio Fábrica) PUBLISHES done-for-you AI fashion prices — R$11,67 per lookbook image, R$53 per campaign image, R$53 per AI persona, R$80–120 per look with video, R$260 per 15–20 s film. The replacement-cost ceiling is no longer an argument, it is a price list. At those rates VBPH's HERO bill of materials (1 KV + 8 stills + hero film + 3 cutdowns) costs ≈R$1.000–1.500, so R$5.900 is ~4–6× the published SP AI-studio price (caveat: Fábrica is e-commerce grade, not premium beauty). WHAT ONE PERSON COULD NOT DO IN 2024 AND CAN NOW: hold one real, consented face across hundreds of stills and 15–30 s multi-shot films with the exact product and a cloned voice (Soul ID; Nano Banana Pro 14 refs/5 people; Seedance 2.0/2.5 up to 30 image refs, 30 s one-take; ElevenLabs Dubbing v2), and run the whole brief→generate→QA loop through an agent. The flip side is identical for the buyer: all of it is self-serve at US$19–149/month, Mercado Livre gives listing photos away, and VestiAI sells Brazilian-model try-on at R$2/photo. So the only things with a price are consent (a real person), a clock (volume on a deadline), and a channel.
